title: Bootstrap percentile and BCa confidence intervals
summary: A stratified bootstrap of the ratio of mean length of stay between two hospitals, with percentile and bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) intervals.

sizing._why: The bootstrap is an interval method, not a design; size for the comparison it summarizes.

pinned_defaults: Stratified bootstrap (resample within each hospital), B = 2,000; percentile interval; BCa with z0 from the share of bootstrap values below the estimate and acceleration from the jackknife over all patients; quantiles R type 7 (numpy default).

Resamples from a shared minimal-standard generator (Park-Miller, multiplier 48271, modulus 2^31 - 1) implemented identically in both languages, so they agree exactly; in practice use boot::boot / scipy.stats.bootstrap with a seeded generator.
_median: The jackknife acceleration is degenerate for a median (exactly 0 for 80 values); this entry first used a median and changed to a ratio of means.
_coverage: Over 100 seeds both intervals covered the true ratio 90 to 91% of the time at 150 per group: skewed means converge slowly, and BCa does not fix that.
